title.narrative: HBP - Ghana Vegetable Fair (Major Fair): Fruits and Vegetable Fair - Organise national horticultural fairs to bring all key horticultural stakeholders to discuss program outcome and related issues e.g production yields/output, product shelf life, varietal issues, taste, market preference etc
Organize a 3 - days HBP - Ghana Vegetables Fair that bring all stakeholders to exhibit and sell their products. A fair that attract at least 50 vendors and 800 to 1000 visitors within the three days.

Organise Regional Horticultural Fairs Channel One TV AgriFair: HBP participated in the Channel One TV AgriFair 2025. It was a 3-day exhibition held from June 20–22 at the Efua Sutherland Children’s Park in Accra. HBP secured exhibition slots for 20 of its network members to showcase their horticultural products and services. The fair brought together diverse stakeholders across the agricultural value chain, offering visibility, networking, and sales opportunities. HBP leveraged the media coverage associated with the sponsorship to share its core objectives, vision, and mission with the wider public. The platform was also used to acknowledge and promote its strategic partners, including IDH and the Royal Netherlands Embassy. The event culminated in strong market traction for member SMEs, including record sales and investor interest. Notably, the HBP project coordinator engaged the Minister for Food and Agriculture, Hon. Eric Opoku, and advocated for Ghana to specialize in a high-performing commodity like habaneros, citing Burkina Faso’s success with tomatoes and Niger’s strength in onions. Official Partnership Launch: There was an official launching of the collaboration between EKN, IDH, HBP and MoFA which coincided with the visit of the Dutch Minister of Foreign Trade and Development to Ghana. There was a mini horticulture fair organised by IDH and HBP. HBP in collaboration with IDH and the Netherlands Embassy organized a one-day mini fruit and vegetable fair at the Fafraha Community Senior High School. The event accorded with the visit of Her Excellency Liesje Schreinemacher, Minister for Foreign Trade and Development Cooperation of the Netherlands, to Ghana. The Minister's visit was intended to actively engage with local authorities and stakeholders in the agriculture sector, to foster discussions on trade investments and youth entrepreneurship. Also, to formalize agreements between the Netherlands and the Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) and IDH, the partners officially signed partnership of agreement. Sunyani Mini Horticulture Fair: As part of organising regional horticulture fairs at regional levels to promote horticulture regional chapters development, HBP in collaboration with IDH organized a one-day Mini Fruit and Vegetable Fair at Sunyani in the Bono Region of Ghana. This event was held at the VAG Parade Square in Sunyani. Attendees, including company representatives, had the opportunity to engage directly with the Bono Regional Minister and other key stakeholders in the sector. These interactions provided a platform for discussing achievements, sharing best practices, and addressing challenges faced by the horticulture industry.
